part_1.title: Power Plant Fundamentals & Commodity Frameworks
topics: How AI demand is exploding — data center power doubling every ~2 years
Power plant types: natural gas (peaker, combined cycle), renewables, nuclear, coal
Merit order dispatch — generators bid marginal cost, last unit needed sets clearing price
Heat rates — efficiency measure (MMBtu/MWh); lower is more efficient
Building a power plant: site selection, permitting, interconnection, fuel access
Behind-the-meter (BTM) generation vs front-of-meter grid connection
Regional market structure: ISOs/RTOs (ERCOT, PJM, CAISO, MISO, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE)

part_2.title: Trading Methodologies & Practical Pricing Models
topics: Locational Marginal Pricing (LMP) — price at each grid node = energy + congestion + losses
Forward contracts and hedging — locking in future electricity prices
Spark spread — electricity price minus fuel cost (gas price × heat rate)
Dark spread (coal), green spread (renewables), quark spread (nuclear)
Heat Rate Call Option — right to convert fuel to electricity at market prices
Capacity markets — separate payment for being available (PJM, ISO-NE) vs energy-only (ERCOT)
Congestion and transmission constraints — how location drives price divergence

case_studies.name: Texas Negative Prices
case_studies.description: Negative price hours driven by wind overgeneration and inflexible baseload; energy-only market without capacity payments amplifies price volatility

case_studies.name: Homer City Redevelopment
case_studies.description: Retired coal plant (heat rate ~10) being redeveloped as natural gas facility; illustrates economics of repowering at existing grid interconnection points

case_studies.name: California Evening Price Spike
case_studies.description: Rising evening prices as solar drops off and gas peakers ramp up — the duck curve in action; NP-15 vs SP-15 split via Path 15 transmission

key_concepts.marginal_pricing: In competitive electricity markets, generators submit cost-based offers. The last generator needed to meet demand sets the market-clearing price (system marginal price). All dispatched generators receive this price.
key_concepts.lmp: Locational Marginal Price = Energy component + Congestion component + Loss component. The Lagrange multiplier of each location's balance constraint equals the marginal cost of an additional MWh at that node.
key_concepts.spark_spread: Spark Spread = Electricity Price - (Natural Gas Price × Heat Rate). A '7 heat-rate spark spread' assumes a combined-cycle gas turbine with 7.0 MMBtu/MWh efficiency.
key_concepts.heat_rate_call: A Heat Rate Call Option represents the right, but not the obligation, to convert fuel into electricity and sell at market prices. Gas plants are effectively long heat-rate call options.
key_concepts.capacity_market: PJM and ISO-NE run forward capacity auctions paying generators for availability ($/MW-day). ERCOT is energy-only — no capacity payments, prices spike to VOLL ($5,000/MWh cap) during scarcity.
key_concepts.btm_generation: Behind-the-meter: power generated and consumed on-site, bypassing the grid. Simplifies interconnection but requires fuel access (gas pipeline spur), cooling, and on-site space.
key_concepts.merit_order: Generators dispatched lowest marginal cost first: nuclear/renewables (near-zero) → coal → combined-cycle gas → gas peakers. Last unit dispatched sets the price.

data_center_demand.note: US data center electricity demand; AI racks require 50-100 kW vs 5-10 kW for traditional racks

natural_gas_context.note: Gas is the marginal fuel in most US power markets; gas price × heat rate = variable cost of gas-fired generation

nuclear_ppa_pipeline.project: Three Mile Island restart + Helion fusion

ercot_characteristics.negative_price_hours: Driven by wind overgeneration + inflexible baseload
ercot_characteristics.key_feature: No capacity payments — scarcity pricing provides investment signal

caiso_characteristics.key_feature: Duck curve — solar depression midday, evening ramp requires gas peakers
caiso_characteristics.evening_price_pattern: Rising prices as solar drops and gas peakers dispatch

energy_pipelines_gas_chokepoint.focus: LNG equity screen — US gas, LNG export terminals, spread beta analysis
energy_pipelines_gas_chokepoint.overlap: Natural gas pricing fundamentals, international gas spreads, Henry Hub as reference price
energy_pipelines_gas_chokepoint.power2026_extension: Power 2026 extends from gas commodity pricing into how gas prices flow through to electricity pricing via heat rates and spark spreads. The gas chokepoint thesis (international gas spread scarcity) is upstream of the power market thesis (gas as marginal fuel setting electricity prices).

conditional_machine_natgas_vol.overlap: Natural gas volatility regime is critical context for power market pricing — gas vol directly feeds through to electricity price vol via spark spread mechanics
conditional_machine_natgas_vol.power2026_extension: Power 2026's heat-rate-call-option framework explains WHY natgas vol matters for power: a gas plant is long a call option on the spark spread, so higher gas vol = higher option value = different investment economics.

commodity_rv.power2026_extension: Adds the electricity layer on top of commodity RV — electricity as a derivative commodity priced off gas/coal/renewables through merit-order dispatch.

cascade_system.power2026_extension: Data center demand shock is a structural demand cascade — AI capex → GPU demand → power demand → gas demand → infrastructure capex. Power 2026 maps the bottleneck at the power/grid layer.
